He is currently the head coach for the [[Maine Celtics]] of the [[NBA G League]]. His prior professional teams were the [[Boston Celtics]], [[Philadelphia 76ers]] and [[Phoenix Suns]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), and the [[Maine Red Claws]], [[Idaho Stampede]], and [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] of the NBA Development League. He also played professionally overseas, notably for [[FC Barcelona Lassa]] and [[Movistar Estudiantes]]. Pressey played [[college basketball]] for the [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri Tigers]]. As a junior playing [[point guard]] for the [[2012–13 Missouri Tigers men's basketball team]], Pressey announced on April 10, 2013, that he would forgo his senior season of eligibility at Missouri and enter the [[2013 NBA draft]] instead.{{cite web|last=Oberholtz|first=Chris|url=http://www.kctv5.com/story/21932032/missouris-phil-pressey-decides-to-enter-2013-nba-draft|title=Missouri's Phil Pressey decides to enter 2013 NBA Draft|agency=[[Associated Press]]|publisher=[[KCTV-TV]]|date=April 10, 2013|access-date=April 10, 2013|archive-date=March 4, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304030851/http://www.kctv5.com/story/21932032/missouris-phil-pressey-decides-to-enter-2013-nba-draft|url-status=dead}} He led the [[2011–12 Big 12 men's basketball season|2011–12 Big 12 Conference]] in [[assist (basketball)|assists]], [[Steal (basketball)|steals]] and assist-to-turnover ratio and was a 2011–12 All-Big 12 team selection as a result. He shares the [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) single-game assists record (19) and was the 2012 SEC Preseason Player of the Year. He earned [[2012–13 Southeastern Conference men's basketball season|2012–13 All-SEC First team]] selection and was the conference assist champion. He earned [[Associated Press]] 2013 All-American honorable mention recognition. He holds Missouri single-game, single-season and career assists records and numerous Missouri steals records, including career steals. Pressey was a [[high school basketball]] All-state selection by the Texas Association of Basketball Coaches (TABC) and helped his team achieve 2009 and 2010 [[Southwest Preparatory Conference]] (SPC) state championships in basketball. In high school, several [[YouTube]] videos of him [[slam dunk|dunking]] (often over much taller players) became popular. He is the son of [[1982 NBA draft|1982 first-round NBA draft]] selection and [[1982 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|1982 Consensus All-American]] [[Paul Pressey]]. ==Early years== {{multiple image | align = left | direction = vertical | header = 2009 Nike Global Challenge | width = 160 | image1 = 20091209 Phil Pressey head shot.jpg | alt1 = | caption1 = | image2 = 20091209 Phil Pressey action shot.jpg | alt2 = }} In June 2006, Pressey stood at {{convert|5|ft|3|in|m}}.{{cite web|url=https://pqasb.pqarchiver.com/boston/access/1049038101.html?FMT=ABS&FMTS=ABS:FT&type=current&date=Jun+05%2C+2006&author=Justin+Rebello%2C+GLOBE+CORRESPONDENT&pub=Boston+Globe&desc=BABC+RETAINS+CROWN&pqatl=google|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130131172625/http://pqasb.pqarchiver.com/boston/access/1049038101.html?FMT=ABS&FMTS=ABS:FT&type=current&date=Jun+05,+2006&author=Justin+Rebello,+GLOBE+CORRESPONDENT&pub=Boston+Globe&desc=BABC+RETAINS+CROWN&pqatl=google|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 31, 2013|title=BABC RETAINS CROWN|access-date=December 30, 2012|date=June 5, 2006|work=[[Boston Globe]]|page=D10|url-access=subscription |last=Rebello|first=Justin}} That year, he led the Boston Amateur Basketball Club (BABC), also known as the Boston Amateur Athletic Club, to the 2006 [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) National Championship.{{cite web|url=http://www.newenglandrecruitingreport.com/news/article/1010/Pressey-Makes-Decision.php|title=Pressey Makes Decision|access-date=December 30, 2012|date=September 14, 2006|work=[[New England Recruiting Report]]|archive-date=November 11, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131111185339/http://www.newenglandrecruitingreport.com/news/article/1010/Pressey-Makes-Decision.php|url-status=dead}} He had joined the team as a seventh-grader in 2005.
